functions.name: m_move
functions.sourceReview: Read the complete selected monmove.c m_move() range (1715-2087), including mintrap and eating order, concealment and set_apparxy setup, tame and shopkeeper/guard/priest dispatch, covetous and mail branches, Tengu natural teleport, swallowed handling, approach and item search, candidate enumeration and tie-breaking, displacement/aggression, region and boulder gates, physical movement, and postmov ordering. The Tengu branch now consumes rn2(5) before tele_restrict(); a rejected teleport falls through to ordinary movement on no-teleport levels, while teleport-permitted relocation remains fail-closed at the production action boundary because its complete rloc()/mnexto() side effects are not yet connected. The selected ordinary movement and Tengu fall-through branches preserve C evaluation and PRNG order; worm movement, covetous tactics, isgd/ispriest special cases outside their admitted return paths, displacement, boulder breaking, and teleport-permitted relocation remain explicit source-named seams rather than invented behavior. The existing mhitu.c attack-call identifier correction is included because the independent production recording reaches mattacku() after m_move().

callers.source: monmove.c dochug() calls m_move(mtmp, FALSE) for the ordinary monster action; moveSimpleOrdinary() supplies the production operation environment and invokes js/monmove.js m_move().

monmove.c movemon_singlemon() reaches dochug() after its pre-action gates; runSimpleMonsterAction() is the production dochugw() adapter and passes moveSimpleOrdinary() as dochug()'s moveMonster operation.

mon.c movemon_singlemon() schedules one monster turn through the elapsed-turn adapter; js/allmain.js wires runSimpleMonsterAction() into that scheduler, which reaches m_move() through the moveMonster operation.

entryPointReview: The selected runnable entry points are ordinary not_special movement and the Tengu natural-teleport branch when tele_restrict() rejects on a no-teleport level; both run through the production dochugw()/dochug()/moveSimpleOrdinary() chain and are exercised by the independent Castle recipe and matching recording. Tengu teleport-permitted relocation is deliberately fail-closed because rloc()/mnexto() operation ownership is incomplete. The source range was traced for the remaining worm, covetous, guard/priest special, displacement, boulder, and other helper branches; their existing source-named seams remain for later source-owner spans and are not claimed by this entry-point evidence.
